ratings_why.fun: Watching pips pile up and then routing them with bats and dormice to tip thresholds is a satisfying draft with a big late payoff.
ratings_why.distinct: Movable, spendable Age is fresher than Hedgerow folk's slot clocks, but the Long Sleep build still reads as a turns-kept tribe.

verdict_why: Two wordings (Echo Bat's target, Mother Ribica's catch-up rule) still make a player stop and work it out; one more pass fixes them.

points.text: Echo Bat's "your youngest other unit" could be the unit being sold, since it is still on board when the Age moves. Say "other than the sold unit and this".
Mother Ribica's "a step it has passed happens next turn" is hard to read. Say plainly: one step a turn per unit; any extra steps wait for later turns.
The fantasy lands well: olms that sit Still, bats carrying Age, dormice cashing it in, and Parkelj the one who moves. Kurent Bellman is the one card whose action doesn't match its folk.
Kurent Bellman could ring the sleepers awake instead, e.g. its neighbours' Awaken thresholds count 1 lower, so the carnival bell does something a reader connects to its name.
The Eldest's Awaken 20 needs the Eldest itself to hold 20 Age; a short reminder ("this unit has 20 Age") would stop players reading it as board-wide Age.

standouts.why: Brother Netopir's relay is the bat courier who serves whoever asked last, and it creates the tribe's best placement puzzle.
Parkelj the Dark breaks the tribe's one rule and freely moves the board, which is the scandal from the lore, played.
Gilled Hatchling is a one-line seed that rewards every way of gaining Age, sitting or relayed.

weakest.why: Kurent Bellman is a plain number aura with no link between the carnival bell and what it does.
Seven-Month Dormouse is a flat 1 gold a turn unless fed, and fights its own Still threshold use.
Cloister Novice works but is a generic "buff the oldest" engine that the Eldest does better later.

flags.note: Awaken 20 doubles the whole board once, golden triples; reachable fast with Netopir and Echo Bat feeding a fresh Eldest.
Whether the sold unit can be the "youngest other unit" is not stated.
The catch-up rule for passed steps needs plainer words.
Dragon of the Springs counts all board Age; with Hrošč doubling it, late fights could swing hard.
